name: lexgen
description: Lexer generator using a Rust macro DSL, alternative to logos

license.comment: Cargo.toml of both `lexgen` (proc-macro) and `lexgen_util` (runtime): `license = "MIT"`; GitHub reports SPDX MIT.

approach.comment: "A fully-featured lexer generator implemented as a proc macro": the `lexer!` macro compiles named rule sets of regexes into DFAs. No parsing facilities; the repo ships a LALRPOP integration example (`crates/lexgen_lalrpop_example`).

implementation.comment: Proc-macro crate depends on proc-macro2, quote, rustc-hash, syn (0.16.0; main adds smallvec); runtime crate `lexgen_util` depends only on `unicode-width`. All pure Rust, no `cc`.

crates-io.comment: Two crates are needed: `lexgen` (the `lexer!` proc macro) and `lexgen_util` (runtime: `Lexer`, `Loc`, `LexerError`), released in lockstep (both 0.16.0).

documentation.comment: docs.rs for `lexgen` contains only the `lexer` macro entry with the note "Please see the project README for usage"; the README is the reference (rule syntax, regex syntax, semantic actions, state, location tracking).

latest-stable-version.comment: Checked 2026-09-19; published 2024-12-24. 19 versions total, none yanked. Research reflects lexgen/lexgen_util 0.16.0 plus the `main` branch (only two small post-release commits).

grammar-class.comment: Lexer generator: each rule set is compiled to a DFA from a regex syntax (character sets/ranges, `*`/`+`/`?`, alternation, set difference `#`, Unicode property classes such as `$$XID_Start`, and a limited right-context lookahead `> <regex>`). Per RESEARCH.md, `regular`.

grammar-definition.comment: Rules are written inside the function-like `lexer! { ... }` proc macro with its own syntax (`<regex> => <action>,`, `<regex> =? <fallible action>,`, `<regex> = <token>,`, `<regex>,` to skip; `let` bindings for named regexes; named rule sets starting with `Init`).

left-recursion.comment: Lexer only; per RESEARCH.md `n/a` for lexers.

ambiguity-handling.comment: Not a parser, so the tag set does not apply. Overlapping rules are resolved by longest match: the generated DFA records the last accepting state and backtracks to it when the scan dies. The README documents no explicit priority/tie-break rule between rules that match the same length, and there is no build-time ambiguity check.

backtracking.comment: Longest-match DFA that backtracks to the last accepting state (`Lexer::backtrack()` restores the saved iterator/location); the distance backtracked is not bounded. A Prolog-style cut/commit operator (`!`) is requested in issue #35 but not implemented as of 2026-09-19; the documented workaround is separate rule sets.

lexer-integration.comment: Generated lexers implement `Iterator<Item = Result<(Loc, T, Loc), LexerError<E>>>` — the triple shape LALRPOP expects from an external lexer; the repo ships a LALRPOP example crate.

unicode-aware.comment: Operates on `char`s (`Iterator<Item = char>`), regex character classes are Unicode scalar ranges, built-in classes mirror `char::is_alphabetic`, `is_whitespace`, XID_Start/XID_Continue etc.; `Loc.col` is a character/display-width column, `Loc.byte_idx` a UTF-8 byte index.

input-types.comment: `Lexer::new(&str)` / `new_with_state(&str, S)` for string input, or `new_from_iter(I: Iterator<Item = char> + Clone)` / `new_from_iter_with_state` for any char iterator (in which case `match_()` panics because there is no backing slice). No byte-slice input.

streaming-partial-input.comment: No "need more input" signal: end of the iterator is end of input (the `Init` rule set returns `None`, other rule sets return `Some(Err(..))`). A char iterator can be supplied, but it is consumed as a complete input.

zero-copy.comment: `Lexer<'input, ..>` holds `input: &'input str`; `match_()` returns the current lexeme as a borrowed `&str`, so semantic actions can build tokens carrying `&'input str` slices. Not available when constructed from a char iterator.

span-tracking.comment: Every token is yielded as `(Loc, T, Loc)` and `match_loc()` gives the same bounds; `Loc { line: u32, col: u32, byte_idx: usize }` (all zero-based; tabs count as 4 columns, other chars by `unicode-width`). Errors carry a single `Loc`.

output-model.comment: Produces a flat iterator of user-defined tokens; no tree.

semantic-actions.comment: Actions are Rust closures `fn(&mut Lexer) -> SemanticActionResult` with access to `match_()`, `match_loc()`, `peek()`, `state()`, and control methods `return_()`, `continue_()`, `switch()`, `switch_and_return()`, `reset_match()`. `=?` actions may return `Result<Token, UserError>`.

whitespace-comment-handling.comment: A bare `<regex>,` rule (sugar for `=> |lexer| lexer.continue_()`) drops the match; multi-line comments are typically handled with a dedicated rule set. Trivia can alternatively be emitted as ordinary tokens.

stateful-parsing.comment: Optional user state type declared in the `lexer!` header (`type State = ...`), passed via `new_with_state`, and mutable from actions through `lexer.state()`; plus multiple named rule sets switched from actions for context-dependent lexing.

error-recovery.comment: On no match the iterator yields `Err(LexerError { location, kind: InvalidToken })` after resetting its match state (PR #49); there is no documented skip-to-sync mechanism or recovery API, and the README does not document what `next()` does after an error. `none` per the RESEARCH.md bar (`basic` needs a documented skip/sync mechanism).

multiple-errors-per-parse.comment: The iterator is not fused and `backtrack()` resets the DFA state on `InvalidToken`, so calling `next()` again is possible, but whether the lexer makes progress past the offending character is undocumented in README and API docs. Left null rather than asserting either way (checked 2026-09-19).

expected-token-reporting.comment: `LexerErrorKind` is just `InvalidToken | Custom(E)`; no expected-pattern set.

custom-error-types.comment: Fallible `=?` actions return `Result<Token, UserError>`; a user error type declared in the `lexer!` header surfaces as `LexerError<E> { location: Loc, kind: LexerErrorKind::Custom(E) }`.

error-span-fidelity.comment: `LexerError<E>` carries a single `location: Loc` (line, col, byte index) — a position, not a range; no labelled spans. 3 per the guideline. (Successful tokens do get start+end `Loc`.)

diagnostic-crate-integration.comment: No bridge to ariadne/miette/codespan-reporting/annotate-snippets in the crates, examples, or README.

contextual-error-messages.comment: No per-rule label/context mechanism. Open issues #36 ("Provide a way to specify error value when failing to match") and #23 request richer failure reporting; user code can only produce custom errors from fallible actions.

lossless-syntax-tree.comment: Emits tokens only; skipped matches are dropped.

syntax-highlighting-queries.comment: No query language or highlighting API.

used-by-lsp-ide.comment: None of the tagged editors depend on lexgen; crates.io reverse dependencies are parsegen, xq-lang, math-engine, lex_sleuther_multiplexer (lib.rs: 9 dependents, 5 direct) as of 2026-09-19.

runtime-speed-tier.comment: Only data point is the maintainer's own comparison (blog, 2024-11-22, JSON-style event parser): lexgen-generated 179 MB/s vs hand-written iterator 274 MB/s and push parser 304 MB/s — 1.5–1.7x slower, i.e. the `fast` band. Author: "lexgen-generated event parser is the slowest, but I think it should be possible to make it perform at least as good as the hand-written one" and notes little effort has gone into optimising the code generator. No independent benchmark found; treat as indicative.

compile-time-impact.comment: No build-time measurements or issues found (checked 2026-09-19). The proc macro builds NFA→DFA and emits one function per DFA state; the macro crate is ~8K SLoC with a syn/quote dependency.

allocation-strategy.comment: The runtime `Lexer` holds a borrowed `&'input str`, a `Peekable<Chars>`, `Loc`s and the saved last-match iterator — no heap allocation during lexing unless the user's tokens/actions allocate. Not documented as a design goal by the project; inferred from the runtime source.

generated-code-size.comment: No measurements found. Codegen emits a match-based function per DFA state (with binary-search tables for large Unicode classes); the issue tracker has a 'generated code size' label but no numbers (checked 2026-09-19).

no-std-support.comment: `lexgen_util` has no `no_std` attribute or feature and uses `std::str::Chars` / `std::iter::Peekable`; nothing in README or Cargo features claims `no_std`.

msrv.comment: No `rust-version` in any published version's metadata or in Cargo.toml, and the README states no MSRV. Edition 2021 implies at least Rust 1.56, but no policy is declared.

unsafe-usage.comment: No `unsafe` found in the runtime crate, the macro entry point, or the DFA code generator (generated code is safe Rust), but neither crate declares `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, so `forbid-unsafe` cannot be tagged.

proc-macro-reliance.comment: `lexgen` is a `proc-macro = true` crate; the `lexer!` function-like macro is the only way to define a lexer (no CLI/offline generator).

build-rs-step.comment: README: implemented as a proc macro so "it doesn't require a build step".

dependency-count.comment: Runtime crate `lexgen_util` 0.16.0: `unicode-width` only. The build-time proc-macro crate `lexgen` 0.16.0 has 4 (proc-macro2, quote, rustc-hash, syn); `main` adds smallvec.

wasm-compatible.comment: Pure-Rust runtime with only `unicode-width` (table-based) and no platform-specific code, so wasm32 targets should build without setup. Inferred — not documented or tested in CI by the project.

async-friendly.comment: `Lexer` contains only a `&str`/char iterator, `Loc`s, `fn` pointers and the user state, so it is `Send` whenever the input iterator and state are. Input must be fully available in memory (no async/partial feeding).

crates-io-downloads.comment: All-time downloads of `lexgen`, checked 2026-09-19 (~22K/month per lib.rs); `lexgen_util` has 267,268.

maintenance-status.comment: Last release 2024-12-24; last commits 2025-12-26/30 (two external PRs merged: NFA/DFA transition merging, CI fix), i.e. ~9 months before 2026-09-19 and outside the 6-month 'active' window. Repo not archived; external PRs still get merged. Release cadence has slowed from several per year (2021–2023) to one in 2024 and none since.

documentation-quality.comment: The README is a complete single-page reference — rule syntax, regex syntax, built-in classes, semantic-action API, user state, rule sets, end-of-input semantics, lookahead — plus Lua 5.1, OCaml, Rust lexer examples and a LALRPOP example crate. docs.rs is essentially empty (points to the README) and there is no tutorial/book, so 3 rather than 4.

tutorial-book.comment: README reference only; no long-form guide.

notable-users.value: xq (jq reimplementation in Rust; its xq-lang crate lexes with lexgen + LALRPOP), parsegen (osa1's LR parser generator, uses lexgen in its tests/examples)
notable-users.comment: Adoption is thin: crates.io lists four reverse dependencies (parsegen, xq-lang, math-engine, lex_sleuther_multiplexer) as of 2026-09-19; xq is the only widely known one.

bus-factor.comment: osa1 (Ömer Sinan Ağacan) has 283 of ~291 commits; six other contributors with 1–2 commits each. All crates.io releases published by osa1.
